newsitem.title: CANADA: Poll sees Liberal majority in Canada election.
newsitem.headline: Poll sees Liberal majority in Canada election.

text.p: The Liberals are likely to return with a majority and the tax-cutting Reform Party become the official opposition in Canada's June 2 election, the latest Gallup poll said on Thursday.

The poll put the Liberal strength at 41 percent of decided voters, close to the level of a recent Reuters poll and the same as the Liberal strength in the 1993 election. That was well down from the 55 percent that Gallup showed for the Liberals in mid April and the 46 percent just before the mid-May televised debates.
The poll put the Conservatives in second place with 22 percent. Reform had 16 percent but was sure of a large number of seats because of its concentrated Western strength.
"The Liberals' strength in vote-rich Ontario will likely lead them to another majority government," Gallup Canada said.

"The strength of the Reform Party in Western Canada, and the recent decline of the Bloc Quebecois (currently official opposition) in Quebec, suggests that Reform will represent the official opposition in the next Parliament."
The poll was conducted May 25-28 with a sample of 1,507 adults. In 19 times out of 20 this would give the same result, plus or minus 2.5 percentage points, as if the whole electorate were polled.

The poll said the Liberal lead in Ontario -- with more than a third of the seats -- was a crushing 53 percent against 20 percent for the Conservatives and 14 percent for Reform. Most analysts suggest a near sweep of the province as in the 1993 election.
Quebec, the next biggest province, showed the Liberals in a tight race ahead of the separatist Bloc Quebecois at 37 percent to 33 percent, with the Conservatives at 29 percent.
For Atlantic Canada, Gallup gave the Liberals a stronger lead over the Conservativs, 22 points, than the 17 points in the latest Reuters poll.
It gave Reform a 12-point lead over the Liberals in British Columbia and 14 points in the Prairies, which includes its stronghold of Alberta as well as less-strong Saskatchewan and Manitoba.
